Here's what this weekend's starters look like for each team:

Brewers: Robert Gasser, Dustin May, Jacob Misiorowski

Dodgers: Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, undecided

Braves: Grant Holmes, Martin Perez, undecided

Misiorowski last pitched Sunday, when he threw 44 pitches in three innings while pitching on four days' rest for the first time since July 7. The first game of the NLDS won't be until Oct. 3, so that would give him five days of rest before his Game 1 start. Like his last outing, it might be an abbreviated one to keep him as fresh as possible for that first October game.

Of note: The NL division series schedules have one fewer off day than the AL series, with off days after Games 2 and 4, so Misiorowski probably would return in a potential Game 5, pitching on five days' rest. In the AL, the Game 1 starter could return for Game 4 on four days' rest. For the Brewers, that also means they will need four starters in the NLDS, when only Misiorowski and Logan Henderson look dependable right now. May has been pulled in the third inning of his past two starts, which could push Gasser into the No. 3 role (Kyle Harrison looks like a complete nonfactor right now).

Keep in mind that the Brewers used an opener in four of their nine playoff games last year, so that's a possibility -- although the more likely scenario is that manager Pat Murphy has quick hooks with Gasser and May and relies on his bullpen.

AL final seeds
Boston Red Sox: 85-74 (vs. Chicago Cubs)

Cleveland Guardians: 83-76 (at Kansas City Royals)

Chicago White Sox: 82-77 (vs. Colorado Rockies)

Cleveland's 1-0 over the Red Sox on Thursday means it's not yet a lock that the Red Sox will play the Yankees in a wild-card series repeat of 2025. The AL Central winner is locked in as the No. 2 seed, while the loser is "battling" the Red Sox for the fifth seed. Of course, due to the wackiness of the bracket setup, you'd rather be the sixth seed, which is the side of the bracket to play the AL West winner rather than the Yankees (and then the Rays).

So, the two scenarios were we go to the tiebreaker:

All three teams end up at 85-77. The White Sox win the AL Central while the Guardians are the fifth seed and the Red Sox the sixth. Cleveland and Boston the season series, but Cleveland gets the higher seed because they have a better record within their division (27-22 so far) than Boston does in the AL East (25-27).
The Guardians win the AL Central at 86-76 while the Red Sox and White Sox finish 85-77. Boston is the fifth since they went 6-0 against Chicago.

Got it? Which leaves the question: How many of their best pitchers will the Red Sox use against the Cubs? Brayan Bello is scheduled to pitch one of the doubleheader games on Friday, but Sonny Gray is done until the postseason and Payton Tolle and Ranger Suarez just pitched on Wednesday and Thursday, so it will be back-end starters and relievers in the other two games.

Statistical races

Yordan Alvarez tries to lock up MVP

This was a Triple Crown chase a few weeks ago, but Pete Alonso has opened an eight-RBI lead over Alvarez, so the Astros slugger probably will have to settle for the MVP Award instead. The question: Do the Astros need to win the division for Alvarez to win? I don't think so. Though we're likely to see a scattered vote, with Alvarez, Junior Caminero, Bobby Witt Jr. and maybe Cam Schlittler all receiving first-place votes, Alvarez is probably the only player who is going to land first or second on just about every ballot.

Caminero has the advantage of having Drew Rasmussen and Nick Martinez as teammates on the mound, while Alvarez had Mike Burrows and Tatsuya Imai. But as hitters, Alvarez has been much better: He has created an estimated 151 runs heading into Thursday's games compared to 107 for Caminero (who also ranks behind Ben Rice, Alonso and Miguel Vargas). And since Alvarez has the much higher on-base percentage -- .432 to 360 -- and Caminero has also grounded into 26 double plays, Alvarez has created more runs while using far fewer outs. He's the best hitter in baseball this year and it's not close. That should get him MVP honors.

Who will finish with the most home runs?

AL: Alvarez, Alonso, Caminero and Rice are all sitting on 41 home runs**. The last home run tie came in 2021, when Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Salvador Perez led the AL with 48. There has never been a three-way tie ... but there was a four-way tie in the AL in the strike-shortened season of 1981, when Eddie Murray, Dwight Evans, Bobby Grich and Tony Armas all hit 22.

NL: Crow-Armstrong and Kyle Schwarber are tied with 45**. Schwarber is looking to lead the league for the second straight season and the third time since he joined the Phillies in 2022.

Who wins the batting title?

AL: Alvarez (.316**) and Chandler Simpson (.309**) are the only AL batters hitting .300.

NL: Luis Arraez (.312**) leads Gabriel Moreno (.310) with Otto Lopez (.304) needing a super finish. Arraez is going for his fourth batting crown, and Moreno would be the first catcher to lead since Buster Posey in 2012.

Will Alonso make history?

If Alonso does hold on to his RBI lead, he'll become the first player to lead both leagues in RBIs after leading the NL with 131 in 2022 while with the Mets.

A few other races:

• NL RBIs: Alec Burleson (112) leads Sal Stewart (110**) with Crow-Armstrong at 107. Not exactly the top contenders in March. Stewart would become the first rookie to lead his league since Walt Dropo of the 1950 Red Sox (some guy named Ted Williams is the only other rookie to do it).

• MLB strikeout leader: Misiorowski leads Cleveland's Williams, 247 to 244. Misiorowski also leads Schlittler for the overall major league lead in ERA, 1.86 to 1.94.

• A swing and a miss: Colston Montgomery tied Mark Reynolds' single-season record of 223 strikeouts Thursday, so he looks like a sure thing to break that. But Schwarber is close behind with 218 strikeouts.

Saying goodbye

This is the final weekend for Justin Verlander ... and maybe Max Scherzer?

Verlander has announced his retirement, so we know his start Saturday at Comerica Park will be the final one of his illustrious first-ballot Hall of Fame career. Verlander has made only one start for the Detroit Tigers this season after returning to the team that drafted him No. 2 in 2004 (the Padres selected Matt Bush in front of him, one of the biggest draft mistakes of all time).

The three-time Cy Young winner looked like a potential 300-game winner in 2019, when he had 225 wins through his age-36 season and was coming off a 21-win and Cy Young season for the Astros. But Verlander pitched only once in 2020 before his elbow surrendered to time and then sat out all of 2021. Remarkably, he came back in 2022 and won another Cy Young Award with an 18-win season and career-low 1.75 ERA. At the time, 300 wins remained a possibility -- and a goal.

But he would go just 22-26 over the next four seasons, leaving him at 266 wins entering his final career start. After Scherzer and his 224 wins, next on the active wins list are Gerrit Cole at 163 and Chris Sale at 159. We're not only not going to see a 300-game winner for ... well, who knows ... but we might not even see a 200-game winner for a long time. Indeed, Verlander and Scherzer will go down as perhaps the last of the true old-school guys who pitched 200-plus innings -- and more at their peak -- year after year.

Scherzer, who has a 6.14 ERA in 17 starts this season, hasn't officially announced his retirement, recently saying he'll have an announcement on his future in the coming days. He just pitched on Wednesday but might come back on short rest to make one final start at home for his Toronto Blue Jays on Sunday. Maybe he wants to try to pass his former teammate on the all-time strikeout list: Verlander is eighth with 3,554 strikeouts, while Scherzer is four behind at 3,550.

The two were teammates for five seasons in Detroit, where they had, let us say, a bit of a rivalry. Here's hoping Scherzer gets one last opportunity, if this is indeed the end, and finishes in a dead heat with Verlander. Then they can enter Cooperstown together.

stories.headline: Oscar winner Lupita Nyong'o invests in BAL team Nairobi City Thunder
stories.summary: Oscar-winning actress Lupita Nyong'o announced her investment in the Nairobi City Thunder, the first Kenyan team to play at the NBA-backed Basketball Africa League (BAL), on Thursday.
stories.body:
Oscar-winning actress Lupita Nyong'o announced her investment in the Nairobi City Thunder, the first Kenyan team to play at the NBA-backed Basketball Africa League (BAL), on Thursday.

Nyong'o is a citizen of Kenya, Mexico and the United States. She is the daughter of Kenyan politician and academic Peter Anyang' Nyong'o - the incumbent governor of Kisumu County - and Dorothy Nyong'o, a PR consultant who is the managing trustee of the Africa Cancer Foundation.

After her Oscar-winning breakthrough in Steve McQueen's 12 Years a Slave (2013), Mexico City-born Lupita Nyong'o shot to fame and has never looked back.

The actress, who notably starred in Black Panther (2018), Us (2019) and The Odyssey (2026), wrote on Instagram on Thursday: "Taking a tunnel walk to celebrate that I'm an investor in the Nairobi City Thunder!

"The Nairobi City Thunder are the first Kenyan team to qualify for the Basketball Africa League, and I'm pumped and proud to be behind them. TWENDE!

"Big weekend ahead with the start of the KNBL Finals! Wishing everyone on and off the court a great time!!"

The team was founded in 1998 - initially as NSSF Stars and later International Christian Church before switching to its current name in 2010. The 2023 acquisition of the club by Twende Sports Limited -- founded by Colin Rasmussen, Sandra Kimokoti, Kush Diriye and Stephen Domingo -- sparked a new era of success.

In 2025, Nairobi City Thunder became the first Kenyan team to play in the BAL in the fifth season of the league organized by the NBA and FIBA - a feat which they repeated in the tournament's sixth edition this year.

The BAL is transitioning to a franchise model from 2027 onwards, with permanent slots in the league on offer along with limited availability for non-franchise teams seeking to qualify.

Nairobi City Thunder will face Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) in the national finals for a third successive year, having comfortably beaten them in the previous two.

stories.headline: NHL betting storylines: Some usuals -- and some surprises -- getting big money ahead of the season
stories.summary: The 2026-27 NHL season starts with a popular Hart Trophy favorite and a crowded trio of Stanley Cup contenders.
stories.body:
Going into the 2026-27 NHL season, there are three teams atop sportsbooks' Stanley Cup winner odds boards, but little consensus of which should be the standalone favorite. According to bookmakers there are distinct cases to be made for each one.

Let's start with the reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes, who are co-favorites for the title this season at +650, according to DraftKings odds. The argument here is simple: This is the team that just won the championship and managed to keep many of the pieces that made them successful last season.

The Canes have actually shortened a bit from +700 when the market first opened, but they haven't been an overly popular selection among the betting public. Despite having some of the best odds, Carolina has garnered just 3.5% of the total handle at BetMGM, eighth-most.

"They can win four Cups in a row, they're probably just never going to be this social darling that always gets money," Caesars Sportsbook hockey lead Karry Shreeve told ESPN. "So you're kind of always safe lengthening Carolina's odds a little bit just because you know you're not going to get that public money."

A team that has been much more popular with bettors in recent seasons is the Colorado Avalanche, who are the +600 favorites to win the Stanley Cup at Caesars. Shreeve's argument for the Avs is that they were by far the most dominant in the 2025-26 regular season and were seen as the consensus title favorites heading into the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs ... but a "really bad eight days" in the Western Conference Finals extended the streak of Presidents' Trophy winners failing to win the Stanley Cup to 13 seasons.

Like Carolina, Colorado returns all of its most important pieces in pursuit of hockey's most coveted prize. The public is largely buying in, too, with the Avalanche attracting a leading 9.4% of Stanley Cup wagers at BetMGM.

"The core is the core, and that core was the most dangerous team on the ice last year," said Shreeve. "All of us [bookmakers] agreed too. The market really raced to see who could get the shortest on the Avalanche throughout the season, almost too much. I think we overdid it."

Then there are the Florida Panthers, who are the standalone Stanley Cup favorites at BetMGM and FanDuel, and the co-favorites at DraftKings, all at +650 odds. Florida opened at a more distant 11-1 for the title, but shot into the favorite conversation after making arguably the biggest move of the offseason by acquiring Brady Tkachuk from the Ottawa Senators.

Aside from the obvious championship pedigree that helped them win back-to-back Cups in 2024 and 2025, the Panthers took solid action from bettors before the Tkachuk trade, creating some instant liability and forcing books to go shorter on them.

"The Panthers are the one team that's probably been just a steady flow of money since the future book's been up, and so it's kind of surprising how we've got this little bit of liability on the Panthers at such a short price," DraftKings Sportsbook director Johnny Avello told ESPN. "They were a little bit higher at first, so that's when some of the money came in, but it continues still to come in on them, even at the shorter price."

To that end, DraftKings has its most handle (21%) backing Florida, while BetMGM notes that it has garnered the third-most bets (8.9%) and handle (6.9%) in its Stanley Cup market.

Who are the other contenders?

There is a consensus second tier on Stanley Cup odds boards across the sportsbook marketplace, and it consists of the Edmonton Oilers and Vegas Golden Knights. Odds vary, but DraftKings lists Edmonton at +800 and Vegas at +850.

The Oilers have taken the fourth-most money (7%) at DraftKings, while the Las Vegas-based books -- BetMGM and Caesars -- report a bit more outsized action on the hometown Knights. In particular, BetMGM reports a whopping 40.5% of handle backing the Western Conference champs, stemming from "notable action," according to the book.

That said, undoubtedly the biggest championship odds mover of the summer was the Washington Capitals, who opened the market at 50-1 and have made it all the way down to 17-1, according to DraftKings lines.

After missing the playoffs last season, the Caps have refueled with newcomers Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou, among others, seeking to give legend Alex Ovechkin one more shot at a Stanley Cup before retiring. Bettors seem to be believing the hype, with DraftKings reporting a fifth-most 5% of handle backing Washington, while Shreeve mentions them as one of the "summer darlings" that took a lot of money in the offseason at Caesars.

The Capitals are causing sportsbooks a bit of worry, but it would be nothing like if one of the popular long shots went on a run to the Stanley Cup.

Caesars' other summer darling was the San Jose Sharks, who check in with 35-1 Stanley Cup odds at DraftKings after narrowly missing the playoffs last season. Spurred on by a young, fun roster, the Sharks have been one of the hottest picks across a number of futures categories going into the season and have racked up a respectable 4.9% of the championship tickets at BetMGM.

San Jose games are also expected to be some of the most popular on a night-to-night basis once the season gets underway.

"The Sharks, given that they're a Pacific team, their games tend to get more action and tend to get more eyes, and there's just no doubt they're exciting games to watch, high scoring and back and forth," Shreeve said. "If they get off to a hot start, we're going to be racing to get the Sharks in the teens [of odds], as I'm sure everybody else is, because they will continue to attract money. So we've got to be very mindful of that."

Given their statuses as big market Original Six teams, the Toronto Maple Leafs and New York Rangers are also as popular as usual across a variety of markets, including To Make The Playoffs, where the Rangers are taking a fair amount of wagers at +235 odds, according to Avello.

Shreeve notes that the Leafs are taking nearly 50% of the Stanley Cup money in Ontario specifically, but it could've been less if the Senators were perceived as more competitive. BetMGM senior trader Matthew Rasp said that the book saw an "uptick" in Maple Leafs money in Ontario after the team drafted Gavin McKenna and acquired Sergei Bobrovsky, but that the Montreal Canadiens are actually a bigger hazard in the province if they find success this season.

The one true long shot giving bookmakers some pause is the St. Louis Blues, who come in at a very long 200-1 for the Stanley Cup at DraftKings. Bookmakers at all sportsbooks polled noted the Blues as a large liability, with BetMGM singling them out as their biggest.

No. 1 picks battle over Hart Trophy

When it comes to betting for the Hart Trophy, there's been one name standing above the rest in the minds of bettors: Macklin Celebrini.

After being the No. 1 overall draft pick in 2024, Celebrini electrified hockey last season between his regular season with the Sharks and his international breakout with Team Canada at the Olympics. As a result, the public is buying into the rising superstar in a big way, making him the most-bet player for the Hart at several sportsbooks. It goes right along with the hype surrounding San Jose in general, for better or worse.

"Celebrini is getting bet to win the Hart at +450," said Avello. "They kind of go hand-in-hand, looking at him to win that and then the team to have a good year."

"If he does slump a little bit, I think the Sharks go with that because there's not that much more around him," Shreeve said.

Past winners Connor McDavid and Nathan MacKinnon lead the way on the Hart Trophy odds board at DraftKings with +300 and +350 odds, respectively, but bettors are largely looking towards other former No. 1 picks to take the mantle as the league MVP.

Avello points out that Jack Hughes (25-1) has been getting some love for the award after his own Olympic heroics, while other bookmakers point to Connor Bedard (40-1) to potentially make the leap, with BetMGM marking him as their largest Hart liability.

The Norris and Vezina Trophies have seen some action thus far but nothing of huge note, according to bookmakers. The same goes to a greater extent for the Calder Trophy, which generally doesn't see much action until at least a week or two into the season, after bettors have had the chance to see the candidates get significant ice time.

The odds leaders for the award are Porter Martone (+280), who got exposure during the Philadelphia Flyers' playoff run last season, and Gavin McKenna (+280), the 2026 first overall pick that is fueling much of the hype around the Maple Leafs. Those are the only two garnering any sort of action at this point, but bookmakers expect that market, as well as several others, to pick up once the puck drops on the season.

"They just kind of wait late to jump into some of these futures," said Avello. "Hockey will pick up its steam, even though football's going. Football, even though you've got primetime nights, you've got hockey going every single night. So that and basketball kind of go side-by-side and, on those football off nights, that's when we'll see the biggest action."

stories.headline: Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga demand FIFA reform amid Gianni Infantino re-election bid
stories.summary: The top leagues in England, Italy, Germany and Spain have issued a joint-statement demanding governance reform at FIFA, amid Gianni Infantino's bid to be re-elected as president in 2027.
stories.body:
Four of Europe's biggest leagues -- the Premier League, LaLiga, the Bundesliga and Serie A -- have called for reform at FIFA in the wake of Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Infantino has vowed to stand for re-election as FIFA president next year despite the uproar caused by the proposal, labelled "FIFA Forward Enterprise," which has now been withdrawn due to the scale of opposition to the idea.

In a joint statement issued on Friday, the four leagues said Infantino had "actively promoted abusive initiatives rather than protecting football from them" and called for fundamental reform at world football's governing body.

As well as the sell-off plan, this summer's World Cup saw a number of controversies involving FIFA and Infantino, including the decision to overturn the red card awarded to United States men's national team forward Folarin Balogun.

"In recent years, football's historic foundations have been threatened by a fundamental governance problem," the statement said. "The FIFA President has actively promoted abusive initiatives rather than protecting football from them.

"And although football stakeholders ultimately succeeded in having the FIFA Forward Enterprise [FFE] project withdrawn, the conditions that gave rise to it remain in place.

"The FIFA President has now acknowledged the need for reform, but considering superficial procedural changes in the wake of the FFE episode is not enough; a profound governance reform is essential to re-establish clear constitutional limits within FIFA and ensure, among other things, that individual disciplinary matters remain unequivocally protected from any political interference."

The four leagues went on to accuse FIFA of "relentless expansionism," saying the body "unilaterally makes far-reaching decisions that directly affect us, such as expanding the International Match Calendar."

They went on to call for "a new governance structure" for FIFA, which would include the establishment of "a permanent body representing key stakeholders, including national associations, leagues, clubs, and players from both men's and women's football," which would "receive full information regarding new initiatives and play a meaningful role in FIFA's decision-making process."

The leagues also called for FIFA's plans to be "based on a clearly defined rationale, supporting data, and an independent assessment, all published before any decision is adopted."

- Gianni Infantino says he is 'committed to doing what is right' for FIFA

- UEFA's Aleksander Ceferin: Trust still broken in football after FIFA, Gianni Infantino controversy

- Infantino accused of 'woefully inadequate' co-operation with probe into Donald Trump links

The FFE project met fierce opposition from European football's governing body, UEFA -- who threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments if Infantino continued with the plan -- as well as Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation.

Earlier this month UEFA vice president Laura McAllister told ESPN that Infantino's plan "struck at the very heart of the principles of the game," with UEFA now pursuing legal action.

The next elections for FIFA president are due to take place in March, at the FIFA Congress in Morocco.

stories.headline: Christian Horner on F1 return: Ferrari team principal would be 'the dream'
stories.summary: Christian Horner has described returning to Formula 1 as Ferrari team principal as "the dream," saying it is the only role he would consider that does not involve a share of ownership in a team.
stories.body:
Christian Horner has described returning to Formula 1 as Ferrari team principal as "the dream," saying it is the only role he would consider that does not involve a share of ownership in a team.

Horner was fired from Red Bull in July last year following a turbulent two years as the CEO and team principal of the championship-winning outfit.

In 2024, Horner faced two internal misconduct investigations based on allegations from a former Red Bull Racing employee, but was cleared in both by independent KCs.

His departure in 2025 followed a downturn in on-track performances and, with six years left on his contract, he was given a substantial payoff.

The agreement with Red Bull allowed him to return to F1 in spring this year, but despite months of speculation around the purchase of a minority stake in Alpine and connections with Aston Martin, Horner has yet to announce his next move.

Speaking to The Times ahead of a publicity tour for his upcoming book, the 52-year-old indicated Ferrari would be the only job he would consider that does not involve a shareholding in a team.

"At this stage in my life, there's only one team for which I would accept non-participation in ownership," he said. "Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula 1. It's the dream. And arguably it's the sleeping giant of Formula 1."

As recently as May last year, while he was still in his position at Red Bull, media speculation linked Horner to Ferrari, but he denied he was interested in the role.

- George Russell leads Kimi Antonelli to Mercedes one-two in second practice at Azerbaijan GP

- F1 teams to expect decision on Qatar, Abu Dhabi and where 2026 season will end by mid-October

- Jamie Chadwick becomes first woman to test drive Williams F1 car since 2015: 'Best day of my life'

In July last year, shortly after Horner's firing from Red Bull, current Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur signed a multi-year contract extension to continue in his role until at least the end of 2027.

In the interview with The Times, Horner said his arrival at a team may mean a significant figure would have to make way, adding that he still envisages a return to F1 in which he resumes his rivalry with Mercedes boss Toto Wolff.

"There comes a point in time where a team's competitiveness outweighs other egotistical stuff," he added. "I'm in a very fortunate position that I can afford to be picky.

"If I don't do anything, I can live here for whatever time I've got left on the planet, and just worry about whether it's going to rain and make the grass green or not.

"But is that going to fulfil me? No. I still feel that there's another dance. And Toto needs to have his hair f-----g ruffled up."

stories.headline: Caitlin Clark: Fever focused on playoffs after blowout loss to Lynx
stories.summary: Indiana is the No. 6 seed in the playoffs for the third consecutive season after losing 86-66 to Minnesota on Thursday.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Forty-eight hours after the Indiana Fever cruised past the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx for one of their best wins of the season, the Fever had one of their worst defeats in one of their most consequential games of the season.

In the regular-season finale, Indiana suffered an 86-66 loss to the Lynx in a game that wasn't as close as the final score indicated. The Fever trailed by 30 points at halftime and 36 in the third quarter before head coach Stephanie White pulled her starters. Four-time All-Star Aliyah Boston aggravated a lower leg injury and didn't return, and reserve Tyasha Harris had to be carried off the court because of a left ankle injury.

The Fever fell to the No. 6 seed for the third consecutive season and will be on the road to open the playoffs against the No. 3-seeded Las Vegas Aces on Sunday. Indiana lost two of three to end the regular season, including a 93-77 defeat to the Mystics, after winning eight of 10.

The Lynx will host the New York Liberty in a rematch of the 2024 WNBA Finals on Sunday.

White said after the game that Boston experienced a flare-up in her knee and didn't play in the second half for precautionary reasons. White called Harris' injury an awkward fall but didn't have an update on her status.

Caitlin Clark was held to a career-low two points on 1-for-12 shooting. Kelsey Mitchell's league record of 27 consecutive games with at least 20 points ended as she finished with 10 points on 3-for-12 shooting.

"At this point, everybody's record is 0-0," Clark said. "We're going into the playoffs. If we sit and sulk about what happened tonight, yeah, it sucks. It is what it is. We kind of came out and got punched in the mouth. We didn't make shots, obviously.

"I'm excited. If you can't get up for the playoffs, then you probably shouldn't be on this team. That's the great thing. You look at one through eight in this league right now, [and] it's anybody's to take. We have to have the mentality going into the playoffs of let's go steal the first one."

Though the Fever were talking about moving on from a disappointing effort, the Lynx had already done so. Coach Cheryl Reeve benched her starters Tuesday when the Lynx trailed by 23 points at halftime against the Fever.

The lack of energy and execution that plagued the team in Indianapolis was gone Thursday, as the Lynx jumped out to a 25-4 lead and never looked back. Kayla McBride, who was held scoreless Tuesday, hit six 3-pointers and finished with a game-high 22 points. Natasha Howard added 21.

"I was just really proud of how we bounced back," McBride said. "Like, it's not easy. Social media, we see everything. Everything that you guys post, Twitter, blah blah blah. I turned it off because everybody's talking about we're 1-4 in the last game[s] and da da da da. We got benched. All this stuff. It's like noise.

"And it's everybody, and it's natural, right? But there's nothing anybody can do or say when we're between those four lines. And I felt like we just came out and we did that."

The Fever went 2-1 against the Aces during the regular season and will travel from Minneapolis to Las Vegas. Though Clark was excited about the playoffs, the team hoped for a higher seed during the season and had spoken about the importance of home-court advantage after losing Game 5 on the road to the Aces in the semifinals last season.

Defense continues to be Indiana's biggest weakness. The Fever are 11th in points allowed per game but have the No. 1 offense in the league.

"This is playoff basketball," White said. "The physicality, the intensity level, the level of focus. ... I don't believe we shoot like that very often. We just have to not let that affect us on the other end. ... It's 0-0, and we're still playing basketball, and so we flush this one. We learn from it, we grow from it, and we start our prep for whoever we're playing tomorrow."

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little ealier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: Arman Tsarukyan elevates his position in MMA divisional rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Arman Tsarukyan put on a performance at UFC 331 that makes him all but undeniable as the next challenger for the lightweight championship.

Tsarukyan has been in this position before. In January 2025, he pulled out of a title fight because of injury one day before he was to fight for the belt. Later in the year, he was twice passed over when the UFC was booking title bouts. But Saturday's elbow to the face of Mauricio Ruffy gave Tsarukyan the impressive first-round knockout he needed to position himself as the likely first challenger of champion Justin Gaethje.

Tsarukyan's victory also boosted him above former champion Ilia Topuria to No. 2 at lightweight in the latest ESPN divisional rankings.

That is the only movement in the rankings, as Saturday's main event winner, men's flyweight champion Joshua Van, already was the top-ranked 125 pounder. Ex-champ Alexandre Pantoja remains at No. 2.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: NRL Preliminary Finals: Teams, line-ups, tips, odds, everything you need to know for the weekend
stories.summary: This is it, the weekend when we decide the two teams that will battle it out for the NRL premiership, and we have been presented with two cracking games to determine the grand finalists.
stories.body:
This is it, the weekend when we decide the two teams that will battle it out for the 2026 NRL premiership, and we have been presented with two cracking games to determine the grand finalists. On Friday night we have an attacking masterpiece when the Dolphins host the Roosters, before Sunday sees the giant-killing Knights facing the biggest giant of them all.

Good luck with your tips.

Friday, September 25
Dolphins vs. Sydney Roosters
Suncorp Stadium, 7:50pm (AEST)

Dolphins: 1. Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow 2. Jamayne Isaako 3. Jack Bostock 4. Herbie Farnworth 5. Selwyn Cobbo 6. Kodi Nikorima 7. Isaiya Katoa 8. Thomas Flegler 9. Jeremy Marshall-King 10. Tom Gilbert 11. Salesi Foketi 12. Siua Wong 13. Victor Radley Bench:14. Connor Watson 15. Angus Crichton 16. Nat Butcher 17. Spencer Leniu 18. Hugo Savala 19. Cody Ramsey Reserves: 22. Benaiah Ioelu

Officials

Referee: Adam Gee Touchies: Phil Henderson, Tyson Brough

Bunker: Ashley Klein

Prediction: The Dolphins were very impressive two weeks ago against the Warriors, restricting them to one try, before unleashing their signature attacking blitz after the break. Previously this season they have allowed teams to get away to big head starts before mounting their fightback, a ploy which just won't stand up in the finals. They appear to have taken note and their defensive work in New Zealand was outstanding. They will need to be at their very best once more against the Roosters, who have the attacking flair to cause them plenty of problems.

The Roosters were simply too good for the Sharks last week, after going very close to beating the Panthers the week before. They have plenty of experience across the park, with Daly Cherry-Evans putting in a much better performance against the Sharks in combination with the hard running Hugo Savala. Outside those two, the Roosters backline bristles with attacking weapons, with Robert Toia and Mark Nawaqanitawase in unstoppable form, James Tedesco always lurking, and Sam Walker returning at halfback.

But, as we all know, the backs don't win the big games, they just determine the score, and the Roosters have a pack that is the match of any in the league. Naufahu Whyte, Lindsay Collins and Siua Wong were at their destructive best against the Sharks. Add the menace of Victor Radley and Spencer Leniu, plus the returning Angus Crichton, and there isn't a weakness across the middle or on the edges.

The Dolphins will have to match the Roosters forwards, with Thomas Flegler, Tom Gilbert, Max Plath, Kulikefu Finefeuiaki, Ray Stone and Francis Molo all in for a big night. If they can negate the Roosters pack, we all know how devastating the Dolphins halves and backs can be.

On paper this is very difficult to pick. It is one of those games that might come down to a key error, a moment of madness, the luck of the bounce or the whims of the referee's six again calls. Whoever wins, we are sure to be treated to an entertaining clash.

Tip: Dolphins by 10

PointsBet odds: Dolphins $1.74 (-2.5 $2) Roosters $2.10 (+2.5 $1.83)

Sunday, September 27
Penrith Panthers vs. Newcastle Knights
Accor Stadium, 4pm (AEST)
Panthers: 1. Dylan Edwards 2. Thomas Jenkins 3. Blaize Talagi 4. Casey McLean 5. Brian To'o 6. Jack Cole 7. Nathan Cleary 8. Moses Leota 9. Mitch Kenny 10. Lindsay Smith 11. Isaiah Papali'i 12. Liam Martin 13. Isaah Yeo Bench: 14. Jack Cogger 15. Scott Sorensen 16. Liam Henry 17. Billy Phillips 18. Luke Garner 19. Billy Scott Reserves: 20. Luron Patea 21. Freddy Lussick 22. Izack Tago

Knights: 1. Kalyn Ponga 2. Dominic Young 3. Dane Gagai 4. Bradman Best 5. Greg Marzhew 6. Fletcher Sharpe 7. Sandon Smith 8. Tyson Frizell 9. Phoenix Crossland 10. Cody Hopwood 11. Jermaine McEwen 12. Francis Manuleleua 13. Mathew Croker Bench: 14. Harrison Graham 15. Lachlan Crouch 16. Pasami Saulo 17. Dylan Lucas 18. Fletcher Hunt 19. Thomas Cant Reserves: 20. Kyle McCarthy 21. Elijah Leaumoana 22. Toby Winter

Officials

Referee: Gerard Sutton Touchies: Matt Noyen, Daniel Luttringer

Bunker: Chris Butler

Prediction: The best team of the 2026 season meets the hottest team of the 2026 finals in what should be another great game in front of a large crowd in Homebush.

The Panthers didn't have it all their way two weeks ago when defeating the Roosters, they were well-matched and needed a wobbly Nathan Cleary field goal to break a late deadlock. Cleary has been the focus ever since, as first he avoided suspension for a dangerous contact charge, and then set about rehabilitating an injured foot. The Panthers have proven they can win games without Cleary, but his coolness under pressure is invaluable in the biggest games.

The Knights are playing with the casino's money at this stage. After finishing last in 2025, making the finals surpassed anyone's expectations. To be playing in the Preliminary Final is an incredible achievement for coach Justin Holbrook and his team, especially considering they are without star half Dylan Brown. They simply have to keep playing the way they have been playing. Fast moving defence, free flowing ball movement from anywhere on the field, and total belief in their ability to beat anyone. Phoenix Crossland, Fletcher Sharpe, Kalyn Ponga, Bradman Best, Dan Gagai, Dom Young, the Knights have weapons across the field. Without Jacob Saifiti, they are a little light on up front, but veteran Tyson Frizell has stepped up in the middle and the Knights back-row ranks, strengthened now by the surprise return of Dylan Lucas, have been simply brilliant.

The big question is; can the Knights execute their attacking style against the best defence in the business? They played just the once this season, with the Panthers winning 44-12. We know how good the Panthers are. We have seen them dominate the big games for years. Cleary and Dylan Edwards orchestrating the attack, Isaah Yeo and Liam Martin leading the defence. The Panthers are the best team in the competition for good reason and they stand between the other three teams and the premiership title. I think they'll return to the big dance this year.

Tip: Panthers by 14
